title: CROWD: City Road Observations With Dashcams
subtitle: A global dataset of continuous urban dashcam driving for cross-domain robustness, interaction analysis, detection, and tracking research.
highlight: CROWD indexes ordinary, variable-duration, temporally contiguous, front-facing urban dashcam segments from publicly available YouTube uploads, with manual segment labels and derived YOLO11x/BoT-SORT pseudo-labels.
overview: CROWD is a hand-curated collection of ordinary, continuous, front-facing dashcam drives through cities around the world, shared on YouTube. Crashes, edited cuts, incident videos and other unusual moments are left out, so the data shows everyday traffic as it really is: the kind of driving that perception models and road-safety research need to understand. The first archived release holds 75,147 segments and 26,274 hours from 238 countries and territories.

resources.title: Dataset deposit

resources.title: Processing and validation code
resources.description: The MIT-licensed codebase contains the download, curation, JSONL conversion, pseudo-label generation, validation, configuration, and reproducibility files.

resources.title: YOLO11x and BoT-SORT outputs
resources.description: Every retained segment has a matching CSV of automatic object detections and segment-local track identifiers for baseline analysis.

faq.question: Does CROWD redistribute the original videos?
faq.answer: No. The dataset release contains video identifiers, segment boundaries, metadata, manual labels, validation outputs and derived pseudo-labels. The underlying YouTube videos, frames, audio, thumbnails, source free text, channel names and handles are not part of the release. The short clips shown here are previews of the footage.

faq.question: Are the object detections manually verified ground truth?
faq.answer: No. The detection and tracking CSV files are automatic YOLO11x and BoT-SORT pseudo-labels intended for reproducible baselines and follow-on experiments, not benchmark-grade manual annotations.

faq.question: What do the time-of-day and vehicle-type labels mean?
faq.answer: Time of day is a binary contextual segment label, where day and night are assigned by visual inspection. Vehicle type describes the apparent recording platform or source-asserted category and should not be treated as independently verified platform identity.

faq.question: Can upload dates be used as recording dates?
faq.answer: No. CROWD provides platform upload dates where available, but the actual recording dates were not independently verified at scale and are not released.
